acceptance: A fake pane that swallows the first Down never receives Enter while the cursor is on No, and boots once the cursor reaches Yes (red first on the current manifest)
The happy path (Down lands) boots with exactly one Down and one Enter
The rules stay bottom-anchored and disjoint from trust_prompt (numbered '❯ 1. Yes'), and the self-match guard test still passes

consumed.resolution: claude-tmux answers the unnumbered trust dialog by observed state: trust_prompt_cursor_on_no sends Down (repeatable, bounded by the auto-respond loop guard) and trust_prompt_cursor_on_yes sends Enter only with the cursor seen on Yes (go/internal/bridge/manifests/claude-tmux.json); both boot waits share autoResponder.bootTick, which re-polls after any send and ends the boot on the loop guard with ExitRespondLoopGuard naming the rule (autorespond.go, driver_tmux_boot.go, recipe_adapter.go), ADR-0118.

fix: Split the rule into data, verify-before-confirm: a navigation rule that matches the dialog with the cursor on '❯ No, exit' and sends Down (may repeat, bounded), and a confirm rule that matches the same dialog with the cursor on '❯ Yes, I trust this folder' (unnumbered) and sends Enter. Enter is then only ever sent with the cursor proven on Yes. Check the auto-respond engine supports a repeatable, bounded rule; if it does not, add the bound in the engine (one rule), not a special case.
summary: claude 2.1.252+ shows the folder-trust dialog with the cursor on '❯ No, exit'. The claude-tmux manifest rule trust_prompt_no_default answers it with one blind burst, Down,Enter. On 2026-10-05 (wave 59's first launch) the Down was lost, Enter confirmed No, claude exited to the shell, the preflight bridge-boot smoke timed out (rc=80) and the whole wave halted with stop_reason=preflight_failed. The rule fires on every fresh worktree, so the race costs a wave whenever it loses (about 1 in 20 boots in the 2026-09-29..10-05 logs).
title: The claude folder-trust auto-response presses Enter only once the cursor is verifiably on Yes
